::: {#thm-level-sets-linear}

#### Level sets of a linear function

Let $\modmemf{\vx} = \dprod{\vcoef}{\vx} + \intcoef$ with $\vcoef \neq \vzero$.
Every [level set](#def-level-set) $\levelsetof{c}{\modmem}$ is a [hyperplane](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-hyperplane)
with [normal vector](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-normal-vector) $\vcoef$,
parallel to the level set $\levelsetof{0}{\modmem}$.
Its [dimension](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-dimension) is $p - 1$:
a point for $p = 1$, a line for $p = 2$, and a two-dimensional plane for $p = 3$.

:::

::: proof
For any $c$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\levelsetof{c}{\modmem}
&= \set{ \vx : \dprod{\vcoef}{\vx} + \intcoef = c } \\
&= \set{ \vx : \dprod{\vcoef}{\vx} + (\intcoef - c) = 0 }.
\end{aligned}
$$

This is the [hyperplane](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-hyperplane) with [normal vector](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-normal-vector) $\vcoef$
and [offset](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-affine-offset) $\intcoef - c$.
Changing $c$ changes only the offset, so the [level sets](#def-level-set) share the normal vector and are parallel.
A hyperplane in $\reals^p$ has [dimension](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-dimension) $p - 1$
by [the hyperplane theorem](linear-algebra-rank-nullity.qmd#thm-hyperplane-subspace),
which gives the point, line and plane cases for $p = 1, 2, 3$.
:::
